description: The octree construction logic erroneously collapses internal nodes into leaves if all their children are leaves. This causes the entire octree to collapse into a single root leaf during a recursive build if the tree is balanced (as nodes at depth N-1 will collapse when their depth-N children are leaves, and so on up to the root), defeating the purpose of spatial partitioning.
code_snippet:
(if (all-children-leaves? children)
                ;; If all children are leaves, might as well stay a leaf
                (octree-leaf ctr sz tris)
                ;; Otherwise create internal node
                (octree-node ctr sz (list->vector children)))
suggested_fix: Remove the all-children-leaves? check and always create an internal node when the subdivision occurs, or implement a more sophisticated heuristic based on triangle count reduction.

description: The ray-octree intersection algorithm traverses children in a fixed order (0 to 7) using fold-left and does not prune subtrees based on the current closest intersection distance. This makes the traversal inefficient as it doesn't visit nodes in front-to-back order and continues to check distant nodes even after a closer intersection is found.
code_snippet:
[(octree-node? node)
      (let ([children (vector->list (octree-children node))])
           (fold-left (lambda (result child)
                              (let ([tri (if result (car result) closest-tri)]
                                    [t (if result (cadr result) closest-t)])
                                   (or (traverse child t tri) result)))
                      (if closest-tri (list closest-tri closest-t) #f)
                      children))]
suggested_fix: Implement front-to-back traversal by sorting children based on ray entry distance, and skip nodes whose minimum intersection distance (t_min) is greater than the current closest-t.

description: The test 'vec-variance computes sample variance' asserts that the variance of the vector #(2 4 4 4 5 5 7 9) is 4. However, 4 is the population variance (divided by n=8); the sample variance (divided by n-1=7) is approximately 4.5714. The test name and the assertion are in contradiction.
code_snippet:
(define-test "vec-variance computes sample variance"
              (let ([xs (vector 2 4 4 4 5 5 7 9)])
                   ;; Mean = 5, variance = 4
                   (assert-true (< (abs (- (vec-variance xs) 4)) 0.01))))
suggested_fix: Change the expected value to 4.5714 if vec-variance implements sample variance, or rename the test to 'vec-variance-pop' if it is intended to compute population variance.

description: simplify-pow can cause a runtime crash due to division by zero when simplifying an expression with a zero base and a negative numeric exponent (e.g., 0^-1). The previous guard only handles positive exponents.
code_snippet:
;; n^m = n^m (small integer exponent)
   [(and (num? base) (num? exp)
         (integer? (num-val exp))
         (<= (abs (num-val exp)) 10))
    (num (expt (num-val base) (num-val exp)))]
suggested_fix: Add a check to ensure base is non-zero when the exponent is negative before calling expt, or handle 0^negative as a special symbolic form (e.g., infinity or error).

description: simplify-quot only checks the first factor of a product for a matching numeric constant to cancel against the denominator. Because make-product-from-list builds a nested binary tree representation, a constant factor in a complex numerator may not be the 'car' of the factors list, causing cancellation to fail.
code_snippet:
[(and (product? numer) (num? denom))
    (let ([factors (product-factors numer)])
         (if (and (>= (length factors) 2)
                  (num? (car factors))
                  (= (num-val (car factors)) (num-val denom)))
suggested_fix: Call flatten-products on the numerator factors before attempting to find and cancel the numeric denominator.

description: simplify-double-angle-product uses eq? to compare symbolic expressions when filtering other-factors. Since expressions are not guaranteed to be interned objects, eq? may fail to identify identical sub-expressions. expr=? should be used instead.
code_snippet:
(let ([other-factors (filter (lambda (f)
                                                (and (not (and (num? f) (= (num-val f) 2)))
                                                     (not (eq? f sin-term))
                                                     (not (eq? f cos-term))))
                                        factors)])
suggested_fix: Replace (eq? f sin-term) with (expr=? f sin-term) and (eq? f cos-term) with (expr=? f cos-term).
